newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israeli spy suspect ordered held 45 days in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Israeli spy suspect ordered held 45 days in Egypt.

text.p: Egypt's state security prosecutor ordered an Israeli suspected of spying for the Jewish state to be remanded for 45 days, security sources said on Monday.
Israeli consul Yehushua Gabbai visited Azam at the prosecution office in the Cairo suburb Heliopolis, they said.
"The state security prosecutor refused a demand to release Azam Azam on bail," one of the sources told Reuters. "Gabbai asked to attend the interrogation but the prosecutor refused."
Azam, 35, chief mechanic at an Israeli-owned textile factory in Egypt, was arrested in Cairo earlier this month by security authorities along with Egyptian national Emad eddin Abdel Hamid.
Hamid was remanded on Sunday for 45 days, the sources said.
"The Israeli embassy's lawyer asked the prosecutor to set any amount for the bail," the source added.

The Israeli foreign ministry said in a statement in Jerusalem on Sunday that Gabbai met Azam in detention. "Gabbai reported to the Foreign Ministry that Azam Azam is well and that he said during the meeting that he is receiving good treatment and suitable conditions."
Egyptian security sources have said Hamid confessed to spying for Israel and receiving espionage equipment. Israel has insisted Azam, of Arab origin, was innocent and demanded his release.
Egypt will this week issue an official charge sheet detailing accusations against the two men, an Egyptian public prosecution source said.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Friday Israeli leaders had squandered the chance to secure Azam's release through quiet diplomacy by making the affair public.
Egypt in 1979 became the first Arab state to sign a peace treaty with Israel but ties have cooled sharply since right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took office in June.
